# prime-progressspinner

prime-rs: ProgressSpinner component (port of PrimeNG)

[Live demo](https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/progressspinner) · [API docs](https://docs.rs/prime-progressspinner) · [Port notes](https://github.com/anton-avramchuk/prime-rs/blob/HEAD/docs/progressspinner.md)

ProgressSpinner — port of `p-progressspinner` from PrimeNG 21.1.10.

Markup and classes match PrimeNG: root `div.p-progressspinner` (`role="progressbar"`, `aria-busy="true"`) with
`svg.p-progressspinner-spin` and `circle.p-progressspinner-circle` inside. Instead of the host `<p-progressspinner>`
a `<div class="p-progressspinner">` is rendered.

Properties are `Prop`/`OptProp`; if all of them are static, the component renders ready values without closures and `RenderEffect`.

```rust
use leptos::prelude::*;
use prime_progressspinner::ProgressSpinner;

let html = view! { <ProgressSpinner aria_label="loading" stroke_width="8" /> }.to_html();
assert!(html.contains(r#"role="progressbar""#) && html.contains(r#"stroke-width="8""#) && html.contains(r#"aria-label="loading""#));
```

## Installation

```toml
[dependencies]
prime-progressspinner = "0.1"
prime-theme = { version = "0.1", features = ["progressspinner"] }
```

The component renders PrimeNG classes; its styles come from `prime-theme` (the Aura theme), one feature per component.
For server rendering enable the `ssr` feature in the server build and `hydrate` in the browser build.
Setting up an application (theme, SSR and hydration): https://anton-avramchuk.github.io/prime-rs/install
